blocking_findings.title: Distinct copied route obligation groups overwrite one another
blocking_findings.finding: actor_surface.v1 tuple omits the subject-group discriminator. analyze_route_policies copies every directly called contract, assigning source=transitive_operation. Two callees may have same entity/effect but different OR subject groups. Their surface IDs collide, and surfaces.insert silently keeps only the final actors list. actor_link facts and original callable contracts can retain the missing rows, and raw canonical policy still binds them, but operation_actor_sources and copied_route_aggregate in route impact no longer represent the exact conjunctive groups.
source_proof: policy.rs:analyze_route_policies clones obligations for every reached call (1000–1020), then sorts but does not deduplicate obligations (1030+).

Checked fixture134 has PrivateNote.summary read subjects [Access.authenticated,NoteRole.owner] and PrivateNote.read_private_label read subjects [NoteRole.owner]. Both produce identical copied surface tuples for an inline route invoking both.

reducer_probe.mode: read-only in-memory reducer on actual freshly checked fixture134 rows copied as policy.rs does; no synthetic source file written/compiled
reducer_probe.classification: Both orders demonstrate last-write-wins; aligned later probe reproduces checker subject order. This is not a claim that the hypothetical appended route was frontend-tested.

blocking_findings.required_correction: Preserve every distinct conjunctive subject group. Either give groups an unambiguous stable semantic discriminator and group-aware links, or represent a stable target surface with multiple sorted distinct OR groups joined by AND. Deduplicate only truly identical groups. Do not union all subjects into one OR group or merely pick the strictest-looking group. Preserve exact copied provenance and original callable surfaces.
blocking_findings.owner_regression_fixture: Append to tests/compile/pass/134_policy_safe_projection.jadpo in an owner-owned in-memory test: route GET /both/{id} { path: { id: PrivateNote.id } success: no_content action: fails NoteNotFound { var summary = attempt PrivateNote.summary(path.id) var label = attempt PrivateNote.read_private_label(path.id) } }
blocking_findings.acceptance: Assert both copied groups retained with requirements_and and each original source witness; semantic reorder stable; paired group change visible and rehashed group omission rejected. No live permission proof required.

blocking_findings.title: Same-entity nonidentity reference changes are missing from link composition
blocking_findings.finding: source_candidates reads the root-only RoleBindingContract.principal / MembershipContract.principal, then attaches candidates for that entity's explicit identity and an equality condition. It does not retain the actual qualified binding/member value reference. policy.rs:referenced_entity accepts any qualified type/reference with >=2 segments and drops all but the root. semantic validate_relationships checks explicit field.reference only; a plain nominal User.alternate_id field type is not that relationship path. Hence changing the same binding/member field from User.id to same-root User.alternate_id can preserve every source contract/candidate emitted here, hiding a relevant actor-source composition change from affected-route comparison.
source_proof: policy.rs:referenced_entity (1574–1578) roots explicit reference.target or field.field_type without requiring identity.
semantic/src/lib.rs:validate_relationships (2880–2905) continues when field.reference is absent; ordinary qualified field types retain their nominal target through semantic/type checking.

actor_links.rs:source_candidates uses facts[role_binding/membership] and principal entity only; principal_candidates compares only the entity identity. Existing facts contain principal_entity but not the exact target field path.
blocking_findings.evidence_limit: Source-grounded reachable case, not a newly compiled synthetic nonidentity fixture. No extra test/source file was written under sole-writer constraints. A full frontend paired fixture remains the owner's regression acceptance.
blocking_findings.required_correction: Extract exact binding/member reference metadata from the already checked AST (explicit reference.target wins, otherwise nominal field type; preserve direct self-identity case). Retain the path/declaration type in source/link facts and compare it against the checked referenced entity identity. Separate source_value_reference_composition from principal-side nominal/resolution identity_composition. Mark nonidentity/unknown composition unresolved/not_identity_reference; do not invent an identity mapping, effective role or live assignment. Keep symbolic equality conditions as required/unproved conditions. Do not implement or relax policy checking as part of this correction.
blocking_findings.acceptance: Paired valid plain nominal User.id→User.alternate_id (same Uuid base, same binding/member field/root) must change actor links and affected route source contracts. Include differently typed nonidentity target where accepted, direct and application member cases, exact absence, declared identity named key and explicit reference precedence. Preserve frontend rejection where it already applies. No checker/runtime policy fix or new owner semantic decision required.

nonblocking_observations.assessment: All checked application/principal/auth_* contracts are copied as entry_authentication_candidates on authenticated routes; public auth:none routes receive []. This intentionally may flag unrelated global authentication contract changes at every protected entry. route_validator_selection=not_resolved, live_authority=not_proved and feasibility=not_analyzed prevent promotion to selected route strategy/live principal. Candidate validator lists may span strategies for a declared variant and remain candidates. No route-selected authority inferred.

Schema5/canonicalization and existing effect scenario ID domains remain intact. Distinct admission kind, null effect and compiler_checked_route_contract certainty are documented and use a separate canonical tuple domain. New actor facets/source comparisons are additive and compiler input manifest binds implementation. No inherent v5 contract violation found; fixes must preserve established meanings.
